title: Desk note: weekly update
bottom_line: Gold fell 2.7% on the week to 3,899, a new 2026 low and the lowest close since October 2025. The Fed held rates on 28 Oct, but two officials voted for a hike, and September PCE inflation came in hot; with oil above $100, markets now price a December hike. Friday's -3.3% was 2.7x a typical day and the worst since 28 Sep. Even so, the close sits at the 15th percentile of last week's forecast, inside the 90% range. Next: whether $3,800 holds and whether hike pricing survives the jobs data.

bullets.title: Fed turned more hawkish
bullets.text: the 28 Oct hold came with two dissents in favour of a hike. Futures price about an 85% chance of a December hike. Chair Warsh also flagged fewer policy meetings per year.

bullets.title: Inflation confirmed the oil story
bullets.text: September PCE rose 0.5% m/m, the most since March (3.6% y/y). Oil stays above $100 on the Iran conflict, which feeds the higher-for-longer rate view that weighs on non-yielding gold.

bullets.title: Not a rates-and-dollar trade
bullets.text: the 10-year yield fell and the dollar was flat while gold, silver and equities sold off together. Hike pricing sits in short rates; the selling looks like inflation-scare liquidation. Commerzbank also points to margin-call selling during the tech rout.

bullets.title: Bottom call
bullets.text: CPM Group expects a low within days of 30 Oct, but says a decisive break below $3,800 would invalidate that call.
